metadata.title: The Ahî Organization A1 — Teacher Guide
metadata.subtitle: 7 short lessons with chapter-specific support, grammar found in the story, and 30-minute lesson plans
metadata.estimatedDuration: 7 chapter lessons of about 30 minutes each, plus one 40-minute review lesson for the end pages.
metadata.targetAudience: A1 English learners: young beginners (Years 2–4) and adult beginners.
metadata.targetLearners: Learners who can read very short, simple sentences with pictures, sentence frames and help from the teacher.
metadata.purpose: Develop A1 reading, listening, speaking and writing through the Ahî Organization: honest work, masters and apprentices, the bad shoes on the roof and the secret of the glass.
metadata.approachDesc: Route in every chapter: Before You Read → Listen → Read → Quick Challenge → Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use) → I can. Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life.

readingFramework.before: Before You Read: one picture or one guess question.
readingFramework.during: The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice. Then learners read and do one small task (underline, columns, act).
readingFramework.after: Quick Challenge, then Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use), then I can and an exit ticket.

cefrProfile.intro: This book is written for CEFR A1. The table shows the A1 descriptors of the CEFR Companion Volume (2020) that the tasks are built on. Vocabulary (English Vocabulary Profile): learners see only A1 words, words with a Word Note and words from the story. Instruction words that the app uses in every book (match, order, true, false, chapter) are taught once in the first lesson. Grammar (English Grammar Profile): past simple affirmative and negative, was / were, there was, imperatives, so, but and never are A1. … years ago, had to, could not, not … yet and because of are A2. The story uses them, so learners meet them in the text and choose them in exercises. Free use is only expected with sentence frames. Türkiye Century Maarif Model English Curriculum (Years 2–8): “CEFR level A1 has been adapted as A1.1, A1.2, A1.3 in Years 2, 3 and 4 for Primary Education.” The grammar route follows the Year 4 (Level A1.3) “Target Language Chunks in Use”: “To be” in the past (was, were), “There was/ There were”, “The Simple Past Tense (+) (-) (?)” with regular and irregular verbs, and wh- question words. Imperatives are in Year 2, Theme 1. The curriculum’s learning outcomes are written for its own themes. This book is a supplementary reader, so it supports these language chunks but does not cover a theme’s outcomes. Young learners (Years 2–4): the curriculum says “There is no analysis or teaching of grammatical structures at this stage.” With children, teach each Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play. Do not read the Explanation lines to them. The Explanation lines are for adult beginners and for self-study.

rows.descriptor: Can understand very short, simple texts a single phrase at a time, picking up familiar names, words and basic phrases and rereading as required.
practice: Before You Read and Quick Challenge in every chapter.

rows.descriptor: Can ask and answer simple questions, initiate and respond to simple statements in areas of immediate need or on very familiar topics.
practice: Chapter 4: act a short talk in a shop.

rows.descriptor: Can produce simple, mainly isolated phrases about people and places.
practice: Chapter 5: say class rules with or.

rows.descriptor: Can give information about matters of personal relevance (e.g. likes and dislikes, family, pets) using simple words/signs and basic expressions. Can produce simple isolated phrases and sentences.
practice: Chapter 2: write about a good person.
Chapter 7: write the secret of a job.

rows.descriptor: Can understand instructions addressed carefully and slowly to them and follow short, simple directions.
practice: Instruction check questions in every chapter (Classroom management).

sensitiveNotes.title: Source fidelity and respectful teaching
notes: Chapters 5 and 7 have Turkish sayings (“pabucu dama atılmak”, “püf noktası”). They stay in Turkish in the story. Do not translate them word for word.
Chapter 4: do not name a real shop or a real person when you talk about bad work.
Do not add legends, dates or details that are not in this A1 book.

grammarSequence: Chapter 1: there was; … years ago; regular past with -ed (helped, visited, checked).
Chapter 2: was / were + adjective (honest, generous); never; so.
Chapter 3: became; had to; could not; too (= also).
Chapter 4: but; looked + adjective; was / were; past forms (wanted, used, bought, went).
Chapter 5: imperative + or …; irregular past (threw, saw, knew, took).
Chapter 6: not … yet; did not + verb; past forms (moved, opened, broke, lost, forgave).
Chapter 7: because of; through; irregular past (held, blew, came, understood).

exitTicket: “It is new, but it is broken.”

metadata.title: The Ahî Organization A1 — Self-Study Guide
metadata.subtitle: Look • Read • Words • Check
metadata.estimatedStudyTime: About 15 minutes per chapter, plus the review pages at the end
metadata.whoIsThisFor: A1 learners who read the story of the Ahî Organization at home or on their own.
learningGoals: Read the 7 short chapters of the story of the Ahî Organization.
Learn the Word Notes of each chapter.
Use so, but, did not and because of in your own sentences.
recommendedUse: The audio is not ready yet. Read each chapter two times, one time aloud.
Do the end pages after Chapter 7.

readingDiary.intro: Write short answers when you finish the book.
prompts: One new word I want to keep:
One lesson from the Ahî Organization:

sections.title: 1. Make Your Plan
sections.text: This book has 7 short chapters. One chapter takes about 15 minutes.
points: Before each chapter, read its “I can” lines.

sections.title: 2. Every Chapter: 4 Steps
sections.text: Do the same four steps in every chapter.
points: Look and guess: Look at the picture. Answer “Before You Read”.
Read: Read the chapter two times. Read it aloud one time.
Words: Tap the bold words. Say each word two times.
Check: Do the Quick Challenge and the Language Focus. Then read “I can”. Can you do it?

sections.title: 3. Look Back
sections.text: At the end of the book:
points: Do the end pages: Knowledge Check, Vocabulary Challenge, Language Review, Final Challenge.
Which chapter did you like? Why?
Tell the story of the shoes on the roof to someone in your family in your home language.
